title: Custom PC Case & Build
summary: A mini-ITX machine designed from the case outward. I came into the project wanting to design for FDM manufacturing first, with as little support material as possible, so the enclosure, the rear I/O bracket and the dual-fan GPU shroud are all shaped to come off the bed clean. Getting a 240 mm AIO, a modular PSU and a PCIe riser into that volume meant working the compatibility, airflow and cable routing problems in CAD first.

title: FDM Printer Modding
summary: The machines that produce parts for everything else on this page, rebuilt to keep up. On the i3-style printer that meant upgraded belts and a new toolhead, a custom fan shroud for part cooling, a bed probe wired into the toolhead breakout, and Klipper flashed and hosted on a Raspberry Pi so acceleration, jerk and input shaping could actually be tuned. Print acceleration went from 80 to over 300 mm/s².

title: Hand-Wired Macropad
summary: A 3×3 macropad wired by hand on a Pro Micro: diodes soldered across the switch matrix, rows and columns run out to the board, then firmware to map it. Small enough to finish in a weekend and a clean way to learn matrix scanning properly instead of reading about it.

title: Curtain Rod Bracket
summary: My mom needed a curtain rod to hang where nothing off the shelf would fit. Two printed halves, sized to the door frame and the load, installed and still holding. Not glamorous, but it is the shortest version of why I like this: a specific problem, a part that did not exist, and an afternoon.
